market_context.summary: One organising fact: a bear steepener driven by term premium, with equities shrugging. The 10y printed 5.315% intraday Monday — a fresh 52-week high and the highest in more than two decades — and the move is attributed to term premium, elevated real yields and heavy issuance rather than to Fed policy expectations. The tell is that Friday's payrolls were weak (prior two months revised down a combined 60k, unemployment up to 4.2%) and the long end declined to trade it, sitting at ~5.25% into Monday before making a new high. This is rotation inside a rising tape, not risk-off: SPY +0.67% to 774.83 with energy and power leading (CEG +3.9%, VST +3.5%, CCJ +2.7%, DINO +1.6%, XLE +1.0%) while rate-sensitives lagged (ITB -1.2%, IYR -0.4%, TLT -0.5%). The regime separates winners from losers more cleanly than a growth scare would: short-duration cash flow and the life-insurer liability structure benefit, while bond proxies, housing and long-duration multiples do not. Note what it does NOT support — long banks, the reflex trade off a steepener, because a rising long end marks down securities books without helping deposit costs. The day's genuine anomaly, recorded and not acted on: Nasdaq and NVDA made record highs with the 10y at a two-decade high, so long-duration equity multiples and long-duration bonds are pricing opposite things.

recommendations.thesis: A $171.5B staple trading at 14.46x forward earnings on a 4.71% dividend yield, 24.9% off its high, because Frito-Lay North America volumes are shrinking. That is a fixable distribution-and-pricing problem rather than a broken franchise, and the fix is contracted: the company has committed in writing to at least 100bps of core operating margin expansion over FY2026-2028, a ~20% SKU reduction, three plant closures, capex under 5% of revenue and FCF conversion of at least 80%. Elliott holds roughly $4B and settled rather than fighting a proxy battle, which is what makes the commitment enforceable rather than aspirational.
recommendations.key_risk: Relative strength says this is still falling, not bottoming: PEP is -19.83% over six months against XLP -1.96%, so it is losing badly to its own sector and not merely to an index that semis are carrying. Consensus EPS has been cut 5.24% in 90 days and the revision direction is deteriorating, so the 14.46x forward multiple is on a number that is still moving down. INVALIDATION, stated concretely: core operating margin fails to expand year-over-year in FY2026 as reported, or PFNA organic volume declines worsen for two more consecutive quarters, or the dividend increase promised for 2026 does not arrive. Any of those means the turnaround is not happening and the cheapness is a value trap. RED TEAM ADDITION — the 3.08 ratio rests on the 106 bear case, and 106 is the softest number in this idea. It is defended as a level 'a dividend-paying staple has historically reached only in genuine distress' at a 5.6% yield, but this same report holds KHC at a 7.33% yield, so a staple trading past 5.6% is not hypothetical — there is a live example on its own watchlist. The bear case is also 12.8x a $8.30 EPS that is itself still being cut (-5.24% in 90 days, direction deteriorating), so if the estimate keeps falling, 106 is a higher multiple than it looks and the floor is lower than 106. At a 100 bear case the ratio is 2.06:1, below the 2.5 long-term floor. The staged entry is the right response and it is why this is kept rather than cut, but size it knowing the downside leg is the assumed number here.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that GLP-1 drugs are a permanent structural hit to salty-snack demand, which would make every multiple here a trap rather than a discount. I cannot dismiss that, and I am not pretending to: it is the reason the entry is a staged zone 6% below the market and the last third waits under 112 rather than being bought at the 52-week low today. What the bear case has to survive is a 4.71% yield on a company guiding to 2-4% organic revenue growth and 5-7% core EPS growth for 2026 — the price is already paying for a good deal of the structural story.

Entry 49.60, stop 46.15, risk 3.45; target 56.50 is exactly 49.60 + 2 x 3.45, giving a ratio of 2.0000 against a 2.0 floor — that is not a level found on a chart, it is the floor rearranged. The stop is on its floor too, at 2.52 ATR against the 2.5 crypto minimum, 0.02 of slack. Both legs resting on their thresholds to the second decimal is the signature the validators exist to catch. Applying the idea's own defensible resistance — the 51.92 50% retracement of the 71.00-32.84 range, which its scale plan already calls the real level — gives (51.92-49.60)/3.45 = 0.67:1. The honest trade is two-thirds of a unit of reward for one of risk, and it does not clear. Note the validator's 'no live price' and 'no ATR' warnings were a transient source failure and are not the reason: I re-fetched at 06:5x ET and IBIT is 48.56, confirming the report's figure. The thesis is cut on its levels, not its data.
